results.requirement: Every plan, including free, shows a support email address and contact form reachable in at most two clicks from any page.
results.evidence: Contact form: ContactForm in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/app/help/tools.tsx posts to POST /public/support in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts, which has no login or plan check. Every public page footer links straight to /help#contact (PublicFooter in src/components/Public.tsx), the app sidebar has Help (src/components/AppShell.tsx), the signing screen footer has Help (src/components/sign/parts.tsx). Browser run (tests/out/audit-support-account/ui1.mjs): landing -> 'Contact a person' showed the form in one click; I sent it logged out and got a reference. Shipped test: tests/trust.test.ts 'support is open to anyone, and an account can be closed for good'.
results.gap: (1) A support email address appears only when SUPPORT_EMAIL is set (default: none), and only inside the form on /help; my server without it showed no address anywhere. /me returns support_email but no screen uses it. (2) The public form page /f/[slug] has no link at all (browser: zero links). /verify-email links only to /app. /signup, /forgot and /reset have no Help link (two clicks via the logo and the footer). The full-screen editor has none (Save and close, then Help, then scroll).
results.suggested_fix: Add a Help link to src/app/f/[slug]/page.tsx, src/app/verify-email/page.tsx, every mode of src/components/AuthForm.tsx and the editor top bar. Print the support address in PublicFooter and in the AppShell sidebar. Make the server log a loud warning (or refuse to start in production) when SUPPORT_EMAIL is empty.

results.requirement: Any chatbot offers 'talk to a person' on its first screen and hands the transcript to the human agent.
results.evidence: There is no chatbot or automated assistant anywhere: a search of /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src for chat/bot finds only copy saying 'No chatbot'. Help is one static page plus a form that goes to people.

results.requirement: First-response targets are published (one business day; four business hours for billing and lockouts) and the target and current status are shown on each ticket in the app.
results.evidence: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/app/help/page.tsx only says 'a person replies'; README.md ('Things to decide before launch') says the pages 'deliberately promise no response time'. GET /support/mine in src/server/routes-trust.ts returns a signed-in user's requests with open/closed, but no page calls it: in the browser I filed a request while signed in and found it on none of /app, Settings, Plan, Inbox or /help.
results.gap: No target is published or stored per request, there is no ticket view in the app, and someone who is logged out cannot see the state of their request at all.
results.suggested_fix: Decide the targets, put them in src/lib/policy.ts and quote them on /help and in the acknowledgement email. Add due_at to support_requests (by topic) in src/server/db.ts. Add a 'Your requests' card (Settings or /help when signed in) fed by /support/mine showing status and target, and a status link in the acknowledgement email for people without an account.

results.requirement: A ticket has one named owner and a visible history; it can be closed only by the customer or after an 'is this solved?' message goes unanswered for 7 days.
results.evidence: support_requests in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/db.ts has only a status column. POST /operator/support/:id in src/server/routes-trust.ts lets any operator close with one click ('Mark as answered' in src/app/app/operator/page.tsx). My run (tests/out/audit-support-account/audit1.ts, section O): an operator closed a request without replying, the customer got 0 emails, and /support/mine flipped to 'closed'.
results.gap: No owner, no history (replies are mailto links outside the product), no 'is this solved?' step, no customer say in closing, no way for the customer to reopen.
results.suggested_fix: Add owner_id and a support_events table; record replies sent from the queue; replace 'Mark as answered' with 'Ask if solved', which emails a yes/no link and lets tick() in src/server/cron.ts close after 7 silent days; let the customer reopen from the same link.

results.requirement: Billing-queue agents can issue refunds without escalation, and support conversations contain no sales offers.
results.evidence: What the software gives: customers refund themselves with no agent (refundOffer and POST /billing/refund in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts; test 'unused signatures from the latest payment are refunded on request, to the cent'); a charge after cancelling refunds itself; a refund made in the payment provider's dashboard is recorded (charge.refunded in applyStripeEvent). The automatic acknowledgement email carries no offer.
results.gap: The operator queue (GET /operator/queue, src/app/app/operator/page.tsx) has no refund action and shows no plan or payment for a billing request, so any refund outside the self-serve rule needs someone with access to the payment provider. Who has that access, and what agents write in replies, is for the people running it.
results.suggested_fix: Add POST /operator/accounts/:id/refund that calls refundPayment in routes-billing.ts, and show the account's plan and last payments beside billing requests in the queue. Write a one-line rule for agents: no offers in support replies.

results.requirement: A logged-out support form is available to anyone and verifies identity by an emailed link or by card last four plus the date and amount of a recent charge.
results.evidence: The form is open to anyone: POST /public/support is registered as 'public' in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts; shipped test 'support is open to anyone, and an account can be closed for good'; I submitted it logged out in a browser (tests/out/audit-support-account/ui1.mjs).
results.gap: No identity check of any kind. Any address can be typed; the server stores the request as coming from it and at once emails that address a copy of the typed text. Operators cannot tell an owner from an impersonator, and the copy can be aimed at third parties (see bugs). Card details are only checked in the separate stop-billing tool.
results.suggested_fix: In POST /public/support, for logged-out senders: store the request as unconfirmed, email a confirm link (signed like stopToken in routes-billing.ts) without echoing the message, and show 'address confirmed' in the operator queue. For billing topics offer optional last-four plus charge date and amount, checked against the provider.

results.requirement: Free users, suspended accounts and former customers (for at least 12 months after closure) can open billing and access-recovery tickets.
results.evidence: POST /public/support in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts checks no account, plan or pause state; SUPPORT_TOPICS includes 'billing' and 'cannot-log-in'. Shipped test 'support is open to anyone...' posts anonymously with topic cannot-log-in and gets a reference, an acknowledgement and a stored row. My runs: logged-out browser submission; a free account and a paused account use the same public route; after an account was purged the same address could still write in, and credits/payment rows are kept so a charge can be traced (audit1.ts sections M, F, G/D).
results.gap: None in the software. Whether anyone reads the queue is covered under the first theme.

results.requirement: Billing and account-access support is never gated behind a paid plan or paid support tier.
results.evidence: There is one support route for everyone (POST /public/support, /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts) and no plan field is read in it; there is no support tier in src/lib/impact.ts (PRICING, PLANS). The no-login billing tools (/public/billing/find, /public/billing/stop, /public/billing/stop-by-card in src/server/routes-billing.ts) are public too; tests 'support is open to anyone...' and 'locked out? stop billing by card, or find every subscription by email' pass.
results.gap: None.

results.requirement: A signer who is not a customer can report a signing problem through the same form and the sender is notified.
results.evidence: The form has the topic 'Signing a document' and takes an envelope id (ContactForm in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/app/help/tools.tsx reads ?envelope=); the request is stored and shown to operators.
results.gap: The sender is not told. My run (audit1.ts, Q1-Q3): a signer's request with topic 'signing' and the envelope id produced 0 emails to the sender and no entry in the envelope's audit trail. The signing screen's own 'Ask the sender' and 'Report' do notify, but they need a link that works, which is exactly what a stuck signer may not have. The envelope id is not validated.
results.suggested_fix: In POST /public/support (src/server/routes-trust.ts): when the topic is 'signing' and envelope_id names an envelope on which the typed email is a recipient, email the sender (as askSender does in src/server/envelopes.ts) and add an audit entry. Give the same answer whether or not it matched.

results.requirement: Billing status (unpaid, disputed, cancelled) never blocks viewing or downloading completed documents and audit trails; only new sends are paused, and only after a grace period of at least 14 days with warnings.
results.evidence: applyStripeEvent in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts only changes plan and subscription_status; nothing in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts (mine, GET /envelopes/:id, /download), GET /export or src/server/routes-sign.ts reads either. Sending is limited by the signature balance (src/server/credits.ts), never by billing status, so there is no billing pause at all. Shipped tests: 'cancelling keeps every signature; a charge after cancellation refunds itself and adds nothing' (export and a new send after the plan ended) and '...a card dispute stops all further billing'. My run (audit1.ts section E): after payment_failed, status 'unpaid' and a dispute, download 200, audit trail 200, export 200, a signer finished an envelope, and a new send still went out on the remaining balance.
results.gap: None.

results.requirement: No account is locked or restricted without an in-app banner and an email stating the reason, the action required and the deadline.
results.evidence: Pausing writes suspended_at and a reason (reportAbuse in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/envelopes.ts; POST /operator/accounts/:id in src/server/routes-trust.ts), emails owners and admins the reason, what still works and how to contest, and src/components/AppShell.tsx shows a banner with the reason. I read the email and /me in my run (audit1.ts F1-F3).
results.gap: Neither the banner nor the email gives a deadline or a review time ('A person reviews every pause' is all). Plain members, who are also stopped from sending, get no email. The error at send time always says 'while we look into a report from a recipient', even when an operator paused for another reason. Other restrictions (first-week daily limit, the payment-notice filter) only appear as an error when hit.
results.suggested_fix: Add review_due_at to accounts when pausing and print it in both pause emails and the banner; email every member; have tick() in src/server/cron.ts chase operators when a pause is overdue; use the stored suspended_reason in sendEnvelope's message.

results.requirement: During any lock, documents already out for signature can still be signed and completed.
results.evidence: Only sendEnvelope in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/envelopes.ts checks suspended_at; completeRecipient, advance and completeEnvelope never look at the account. My run (audit1.ts): a signer finished while the account was paused (F7, 200), while it was 'unpaid' (E6) and after a dispute (E12); during the closing grace period the signer's copy still opened (G4).
results.gap: No shipped test pins this down (the pause test only checks send is refused and export works).
results.suggested_fix: Add an assertion to tests/trust.test.ts that signAll succeeds on a paused account.

results.requirement: Account closure is a soft delete: the owner can restore the account and all documents self-serve for 90 days, and closure requires explicit confirmation and sends an email with an undo link.
results.evidence: POST /me/delete in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts asks for the password, sets closing_at 30 days ahead (CLOSE_GRACE_DAYS in src/lib/policy.ts) and emails 'Sign in to keep my account'; /auth/login in src/server/routes-account.ts clears it. Shipped test 'support is open to anyone, and an account can be closed for good' covers close, restore and purge; my run G1-G2 read the email.
results.gap: 30 days, not 90. The same dialog has a tick box 'Delete everything right now... This cannot be undone' (now:true runs purgeUser at once: no grace, no undo). Nothing is sent before the purge runs (0 emails in my run).
results.suggested_fix: Raise CLOSE_GRACE_DAYS (the pages read it from policy.ts). Make 'delete now' confirm through an emailed link or keep a restorable copy for a short period. Send reminders 7 days and 1 day before purge from tick().

results.requirement: Every plan, including free, has an 'Export everything' action that produces a ZIP of all signed PDFs, audit certificates and a CSV index at no extra cost.
results.evidence: GET /export in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts streams signed/*.pdf (each with its certificate), audit/*.json, envelopes.csv and README.txt; no plan is read. Buttons: 'Export everything (ZIP)' on src/app/app/envelopes/page.tsx and Settings, Your data. Shipped test 'everything can be exported, and the sender sees whether emails went out'. My run (audit1.ts M2-M4): a free-plan account with paying switched on got signed PDF, audit files, CSV and README; a selection export worked.
results.gap: None for the requirement. Small print: a plain member's 'everything' is only what they sent; drafts and templates are not included.

results.requirement: After cancellation, payment failure or closure, read-only access and export remain available for at least 12 months, and a download link is emailed before any deletion.
results.evidence: Cancellation and failed payment: nothing is removed or locked, with no time limit (tests and my section E run under the account-lock theme). Closure: purgeClosedAccounts in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts removes the account after 30 days.
results.gap: On closure the data lives 30 days, not 12 months. During those days the owner is signed out and the only way in is to sign in, which cancels the closure, so exporting means un-closing and closing again. No export or download link is emailed at closing or before the purge (my run: 0 emails at purge).
results.suggested_fix: At closing, email a signed, expiring export link (a token like stopToken in routes-billing.ts on a public export route) and again a week before purge; or allow a read-only sign-in during the grace period with a separate 'Restore' button; lengthen the period.

results.requirement: No document is deleted by a retention rule without notice to its owner at least 30 days ahead with a download link; the retention date is shown on each document.
results.evidence: There are no retention rules: nothing in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src mentions retention, and tick() in src/server/cron.ts only expires, reminds and purges accounts their owner closed. A document goes only when a person deletes it or closes the account.
results.gap: Related, not a retention rule: a sender can delete a completed envelope and the signers' links die without the signers being told (see overclaims).

results.requirement: The account shows a total document count, and completed documents can be auto-synced to a connected cloud drive.
results.evidence: Count: GET /reports/summary in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts and src/app/app/reports/page.tsx show 'Envelopes sent' and a count per status (browser run: 'Envelopes sent 3'); the home page shows drafts, waiting and completed.
results.gap: No cloud drive sync exists (README.md lists Google Drive under 'not built'); the only route is webhooks plus the API for people who can write code. The Envelopes list itself shows at most 'the 200 most recently updated', not a total.
results.suggested_fix: Add a drive connector that uploads the final PDF in completeEnvelope (src/server/envelopes.ts), or at least a documented no-code recipe using the envelope.completed webhook. Show the total on the Envelopes page.

results.requirement: Documents, templates and the subscription belong to the workspace, not to an individual login; a paid workspace with only one owner shows a persistent prompt to add a second owner.
results.evidence: Envelopes and templates carry account_id and the subscription sits on accounts (/home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/db.ts); a removed member's work passes on (DELETE /account/members/:id in src/server/routes-account.ts; test 'a team never loses documents when someone leaves, and ownership can move'). A warning 'This account depends on one person' exists in Team() in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx (seen in the browser).
results.gap: The prompt lives only on Settings, Team; the home page and shell show nothing (browser check), although /me already returns the admin count. It asks for a second admin: there can be only one owner, and an admin cannot take ownership (POST /account/transfer-owner is owner-only), so the account can still end up behind one mailbox.
results.suggested_fix: Show the warning in AppShell while me.admins < 2 on a paid plan. Allow two owners, or let an admin claim ownership after a waiting period with emails to the owner.

results.requirement: A logged-out 'stop billing' flow verifies the payer by card last four plus the amount and date of a recent charge and turns off renewal without access to the login mailbox.
results.evidence: POST /public/billing/stop-by-card in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts and StopByCard in src/app/help/tools.tsx stop the renewal with no login and no mailbox; test 'locked out? stop billing by card, or find every subscription by email'. My run N1 repeated it.
results.gap: It checks the account email plus the last four digits only: no amount, no date. Any member's address works, not just an admin's (my run used a plain member). Last four digits are printed on receipts, and the guess limit is 5 an hour per address held in memory. The effect is limited (renewal off, admins emailed, can be resumed).
results.suggested_fix: Ask for the date and amount of a recent charge as well and compare with the payments table before calling cancelPlan; keep the failed-guess count in the database.

results.requirement: Workspace ownership can be recovered by domain verification (DNS record) or documented company proof, with a published turnaround time.
results.evidence: Nothing in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src does this. /help ('I cannot log in') says only 'write to us and a person will help with the account'. The operator routes in src/server/routes-trust.ts cover requests, reports and pausing; none can move ownership, so a person helping would have to edit the database.
results.gap: No DNS or proof-based recovery, no operator tool, no published process or time.
results.suggested_fix: Add an operator action that makes a named member (or a newly invited address) the owner, with emails to every existing admin and a waiting period; publish what proof is accepted and how long it takes on /help. DNS TXT verification for the owner's email domain can follow.

results.requirement: Changing the login email requires a second factor other than the old inbox and can be reverted for 30 days.
results.evidence: The login email cannot be changed at all: PATCH /me in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts never writes email (my run audit2.ts 3a: the address was unchanged after sending one), and the Profile tab has no email field (browser check).
results.gap: The bad outcome named in the complaint (an email changed and not revertible) cannot happen, but the wider problem gets worse: someone whose mailbox is going away cannot move their login, and password reset keeps going to the dead address. The only route is inviting a new address and handing ownership over, which makes a second identity.
results.suggested_fix: Add an email change in routes-account.ts: require the current password, confirm through a link sent to the new address, notify the old one, keep previous_email for 30 days with a one-click revert link.

results.requirement: A role that needs a paid seat says so at the moment it is assigned.
results.evidence: There are no paid seats: the price is per signature (PRICING in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/lib/impact.ts) and the Team tab states 'there is no charge per person'.

results.requirement: A 'Remove member' flow moves all of the person's sent documents, drafts, templates and folders to a chosen successor in one action with folder structure preserved; in-flight documents stay signable and notifications go to the successor.
results.evidence: DELETE /account/members/:id?to= in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts and the 'Remove and hand over' dialog in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx. Shipped test 'a team never loses documents when someone leaves...' covers the default successor. My run (audit1.ts H5-H10) with a chosen successor: draft, template, in-flight (folder kept) and completed envelopes all moved; the in-flight one was then signed and the completion email went to the successor.
results.gap: Bulk batches are not handed over (bulk_batches.sender_id is left), so a non-admin successor gets 'Batch not found' on the batch page and on its remind/void actions. The hand-over leaves no audit entry. A wrong successor id silently falls back to the remover. The removed person's login is left unusable (see bugs).
results.suggested_fix: In the same handler also update bulk_batches.sender_id, write an audit entry per envelope ('Handed over from X to Y'), reject an unknown ?to=, and run it in one transaction.

results.requirement: An admin can view and download the documents of a deactivated member at any time.
results.evidence: mine() and GET /envelopes in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts give admins every envelope in the account. My run (audit1.ts H4, H11): the admin downloaded the member's completed document before and after removing them (200 both times). Test 'accounts are isolated... members see only their own envelopes' pins the member/admin split.
results.gap: After removal the documents show the successor as sender and the removed person disappears from the 'Sent by' filter, so they can no longer be picked out as that person's.
results.suggested_fix: Keep the original sender in a column (original_sender_id) and offer it in the filter.

results.requirement: Templates live in a workspace library with per-template roles (use, edit, manage); an admin can always edit or archive any template.
results.evidence: Templates are shared with the whole team (mine() in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts skips the sender check for templates) and an admin can edit any of them (my run audit2.ts 4c: 200).
results.gap: No per-template roles: every plain member can rewrite or delete any template (my runs: J11 edit 200, 4a delete 200 and the template was gone). There is no archive, only permanent delete.
results.suggested_fix: Add a template permission (at least 'who may edit': everyone or admins and the author) checked in PUT and DELETE /envelopes/:id for kind=template, and an archived flag instead of delete.

results.requirement: Removing a member frees the seat immediately and the screen says so.
results.evidence: There are no seats to free: nothing is charged per person (PRICING in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/lib/impact.ts; the Team tab says so).

results.requirement: There is exactly one identity per email address; signing a document never creates a separate hidden account.
results.evidence: users.email is UNIQUE and case-insensitive (/home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/db.ts); /auth/signup answers 409 for an existing address (src/server/routes-account.ts); nothing in src/server/routes-sign.ts creates a user. My run (audit1.ts K1-K2): signing up again with different capitals got 409; a stranger signing a document created 0 user rows.
results.gap: None for the requirement. A different identity problem exists: a removed member's login is dead for good (see bugs).

results.requirement: One identity can belong to several workspaces, with a workspace switcher always visible and the last-used workspace opened by default.
results.evidence: memberships is many-to-many, POST /auth/switch changes workspace (/home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts) and the sidebar shows a switcher when there is more than one (src/components/AppShell.tsx). My run K4-K10 and the browser run (ui2.mjs) confirmed joining a second workspace and switching.
results.gap: Sign-in always opens the oldest workspace (ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1 in /auth/login). Someone with their own empty workspace who then joins a company lands in the empty one every time (browser: 'FRESH LOGIN opens: Kim's workspace'), which is the complaint itself. On a phone the switcher and the workspace name are hidden until Menu is opened.
results.suggested_fix: Store last_account_id on users in /auth/switch and /invites/accept and use it in /auth/login; show the workspace name in the mobile top bar.

results.requirement: A single inbox lists every document sent to that email across all workspaces.
results.evidence: GET /inbox in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts selects by recipient email across every account, once the address is confirmed; screen src/app/app/inbox/page.tsx. My run (audit1.ts L1-L2): documents from two different sending accounts appeared in the one inbox, identical whichever workspace was active; an unconfirmed address got nothing (A4).
results.gap: None. No shipped test covers the inbox.
results.suggested_fix: Add an inbox test to tests/trust.test.ts.

results.requirement: Granting a role picks from existing members; entering an email that matches an existing user never creates a second user.
results.evidence: Roles are changed with a select on each existing member row (PATCH /account/members/:id, /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts; Team() in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx). Inviting an address that already has a login attaches the existing user (POST /invites/accept); signing up with it is refused. My run K3-K5: 409 on sign-up, accept 200, still 1 user row. Browser run: an existing user followed the invitation, signed in and landed in the team with both workspaces listed.
results.gap: The invitation link always opens the sign-up form, so an existing user first sees 'An account with this email already exists' and has to find the small 'Sign in' link.
results.suggested_fix: In POST /account/invites, link to /login?invite=... when the address already has a user.

results.requirement: Admins have an 'All documents' view with one search across every sender, filterable by sender, status, template and date, with optional team-scoped visibility.
results.evidence: GET /envelopes in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts shows admins the whole account with one search, a 'Sent by' filter, status tabs and folders (src/app/app/envelopes/page.tsx). My run J2-J5 and the browser run: an admin found another member's envelope by recipient and by document text and filtered by sender; shipped test 'small things that stop people getting stuck' checks the sender filter.
results.gap: No filter by template or by date (my run J6-J7: those parameters change nothing). No team-scoped visibility: members see only their own, admins see everything, nothing in between. Rows do not say who sent each envelope (the API returns it; the table does not show it). The list stops at 200 with no paging.
results.suggested_fix: Add from/to and template_id to GET /envelopes and to the filter bar; add a 'Sent by' column for admins; add paging; consider a 'manager' role limited to chosen members.

results.requirement: The document list has full-text search, folders or tags, and filters that persist after a document is opened and closed.
results.evidence: Search covers subject, people, document names and the text inside uploaded PDFs (GET /envelopes in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts; text stored by storeUpload); shipped test 'envelopes can be found by the words inside their documents'. Folders: PATCH /envelopes/:id and the Move dialog. Persistence: restore() in src/app/app/envelopes/page.tsx keeps tab, search, folder and sender in localStorage. Browser run (ui1.mjs): chose 'Waiting for others' plus a search, opened an envelope, came back by Back and by the sidebar; tab and search were still set both times.
results.gap: None for the requirement. Scanned PDFs have no text to search (flagged at upload).

results.requirement: Each row shows who has not yet signed and offers one-click remind, resend and download.
results.evidence: The list has a 'Waiting on' column (waitingOn in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/components/sender/lib.ts) and a one-click Remind on waiting rows; completed rows have Download (src/app/app/envelopes/page.tsx). Browser run: rows read 'Dee Careful for less than an hour' with Remind, and Remind answered 'Reminder emailed to 1 person'.
results.gap: There is no resend separate from Remind: a signer who switched reminders off cannot be re-sent from the row (the toast says to open the envelope), and a completed copy cannot be re-sent to a recipient from the list. Download is offered only on completed rows. With a signing order, 'Waiting on' names only whoever has it now, not everyone still to sign.
results.suggested_fix: Add a row menu with 'Send the link again' (uses the 'resent' notice in notifyRecipient, which ignores muting because the sender asked) and 'Download' on every sent row; list later signers in a tooltip.

bugs.title: A removed team member can never sign in, sign up or be invited again
bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-account.ts: POST /auth/login (membership check), DELETE /account/members/:id, POST /auth/signup, POST /invites/accept; also purgeUser in src/server/routes-trust.ts
bugs.detail: Someone who joined through an invitation has no workspace of their own. After an admin removes them, login answers 403 'This user no longer belongs to any account', sign-up answers 409 'An account with this email already exists', and a fresh invitation cannot be accepted because accepting needs a session. Password reset does not help. Their inbox of documents sent to them is unreachable too. The same dead end hits teammates of an account its owner deleted. Reproduce: tests/out/audit-support-account/audit1.ts section B (B1-B5) and audit2.ts 7g. Fix: when a user has no membership at login, create a personal workspace (as sign-up does), or do it at removal time.

bugs.title: Anyone can read another person's support messages by registering their email without confirming it
bugs.detail: The query is 'WHERE user_id=? OR email=?' and does not require the address to be confirmed. Reproduce (audit1.ts A1-A3): a logged-out person files a request from victim@example.com; an attacker signs up with victim@example.com (no confirmation needed to sign in) and GET /api/support/mine returns the victim's full message. Affects signers and former customers: after an account is purged the address is free again and its old requests are still in the table (D4, D8). Fix: match on email only when email_verified is set.

bugs.title: The caller chooses the IP address used for rate limits and written into the audit trail
bugs.detail: The leftmost X-Forwarded-For value is trusted. Most proxies append, so the leftmost value is whatever the client sent. On my dev server: 12 contact-form posts with a different header each time were all accepted, while 10 with a fixed header hit 429 at the ninth; a signer request with 'X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9' was recorded in the envelope's audit trail with ip=9.9.9.9 (that IP is printed on the certificate; audit2.ts section 6 shows the same in-process). Every per-IP limit (support form, find-my-subscription emails, sign-up, code redemption) can be bypassed and a signer can forge 'where they signed from'. Fix: take the address from the platform's trusted header or the right-most hop behind a configured number of proxies.

bugs.title: The contact form sends attacker-written text to any email address under our name
bugs.detail: The acknowledgement goes to whatever address is typed and repeats the typed message (up to 5,000 characters, links and phone numbers included) under the heading 'A person will reply to you'. Reproduce (audit1.ts section C): a post with email=target@example.org and a fake payment warning produced an email to that third party containing the text; with the header trick above, 20 more were accepted in a row. Fix: do not echo the message to unconfirmed addresses; send a confirm link instead.

bugs.title: A paused account can still email new people
bugs.detail: Only sendEnvelope checks the pause. Reproduce (audit1.ts F8-F9): with sending paused, PUT /envelopes/:id on an envelope already out, adding a brand-new signer, returned 200 and the new person got a signing request; reminders also went out to 2 people. A sender paused for suspected phishing keeps reaching new victims through any envelope that is still open. Fix: refuse added or changed recipients, and reminders, while suspended_at is set.

bugs.title: 'Deleted for good' leaves names, emails, IP addresses and signer uploads behind
bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts: purgeUser, removeUnusedBlobs; also DELETE /envelopes/:id in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts
bugs.detail: After closing with 'delete now' (tests/out/audit-support-account/audit3.ts) and after the 30-day purge (audit1.ts D2-D5): the audit rows of the deleted envelopes remain (signer names, emails, IPs), the stored copy of every email remains (emails table, full HTML), files signers uploaded as attachments remain on disk and in the files table (they have no account id), and support requests and credit rows remain. Only the uploaded and signed PDFs go. Deleting a single completed envelope leaves its signed PDF on disk and its audit rows (audit2.ts 2f-2g). Fix: delete audit, emails, retired_tokens, idempotency keys, signer attachment files and their blobs for the account's envelopes inside purgeUser and the envelope delete.

bugs.title: A closed account's API keys keep working, and people can still be invited into it
bugs.detail: Closing deletes sessions but not API keys, and closing_at is never checked. Reproduce (audit2.ts section 7, audit1.ts G3): during the grace period a key still exported, invited a new member, and that member joined and sent an envelope with no sign the account was closing; when the purge ran, their envelope was deleted and their login became unusable. Fix: disable keys while closing_at is set, refuse invites and sends, and have the purge skip or hand over accounts that gained members.

bugs.title: An admin can remove themselves through the API and keeps receiving the team's signed documents
bugs.detail: The screen hides the button, the API does not check. The successor defaults to the caller, who is the person being removed, so their envelopes stay assigned to them. Reproduce (audit1.ts section I): after self-removal a client signed and 'Completed: ...' with the PDF went to the departed admin's address. Fix: reject removing yourself, or require a different successor.

bugs.title: Handing over a removed member's work misses their bulk batches and leaves no trace
bugs.detail: bulk_batches.sender_id is not reassigned: a non-admin successor gets 404 on GET /bulk/:id and on batch remind/void (audit1.ts H8), although the envelopes show 'Part of a bulk send'. No audit entry records the hand-over, and envelopes completed afterwards name the successor as sender.

bugs.title: Any plain member can delete or rewrite every shared template, and sees other members' folder and batch names
bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts: mine(), DELETE and PUT /envelopes/:id, GET /envelopes (folders), GET /bulk
bugs.detail: A member deleted the owner's template (audit2.ts 4a, permanent, no undo) and edited another member's (audit1.ts J11). GET /envelopes returns every folder name in the account to a member who can see none of the envelopes in them (J9), and GET /bulk lists other members' batches (J10), despite 'Members see what they sent'.

bugs.title: A public form on a paused or unconfirmed account tells visitors about the abuse review and leaves stray drafts
bugs.detail: When sendEnvelope refuses, the visitor is shown the sender's own error: 'Sending is paused on this account while we look into a report from a recipient...' (audit1.ts F10). The envelope copied for the attempt is not removed, so each try leaves a draft holding the visitor's name and email in the owner's account (F10b). Fix: check the account before copying, show the polite 'cannot take new signatures right now' text, and delete the copy on failure.

bugs.title: Support references can start with a dash or underscore
bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts: POST /public/support (ref = last 8 characters of the id, upper-cased)
bugs.detail: My runs produced '-7Y9WXDN' and '9BC-R7AY'. The subject line reads 'We got your message (-7Y9WXDN)'. Hard to read out, and upper-casing a random id tail means the reference cannot be matched back exactly. Use a short code from an unambiguous alphabet, as checkCode does.

bugs.title: Starting the dev server with NEXT_DIST_DIR rewrites tsconfig.json
bugs.detail: Running 'next dev' as the audit instructions describe added two '.next-audit-support-account/...' lines to the tracked tsconfig.json. I removed my two lines after stopping the server and deleting the build folder. Two lines for '.next-audit-signer' from another audit's server were still in the file when I finished; I left those alone.

overclaims.claim: 'After that date the account, its documents and its audit trails are removed for good' and 'Your account and everything in it has been deleted.'

results.requirement: A signer can open, sign and download a document from the emailed link with no account, password or app install, on every plan including free and trial.
results.evidence: Every /sign/:token route in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-sign.ts is registered 'public' and authorised only by the link token (find()); the screen is an ordinary web page (src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx). Repo test tests/flow.test.ts 'full signing flow: order, access code, completion, certificate, verification' signs with cookie-less clients. Own checks: tests/out/audit-signer/api1.ts S1 on a free account with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY set (signatures counted): open 200, download before consent 200, complete 200, download after 200 (%PDF), no cookie ever set on the signer. tests/out/audit-signer/phone1.mjs ran the whole flow in fresh Chromium profiles (Pixel 7 and iPhone 13 settings) with zero cookies and only /api/sign/* and /api/me calls.

results.requirement: No sender, admin or API setting can require a signer to log in to an account; stronger identity uses a one-time code instead.
results.evidence: No setting can demand a login: the recipients table (src/server/db.ts) and the API Recipient schema (src/server/openapi.ts) hold only access_code, routes-sign.ts never reads the users table, and a search of src for login/SSO requirements on signers finds nothing. The access code path works (tests/flow.test.ts; browser run tests/out/audit-signer/draw.mjs unlocked with 4242 and finished).
results.gap: The stronger identity is a fixed code the sender invents and passes on personally, not a one-time code. Any length is accepted (a 1-character code was accepted, api2.ts S10). With 8 tries per 15 minutes and no permanent lock, a 4-digit code can be tried exhaustively in under two weeks by anyone holding the link, for example the other person at a shared inbox, which is where the editor recommends access codes.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts writeContent() and correctRecipient(): refuse access codes shorter than 6 characters. src/server/routes-sign.ts POST /sign/:token/unlock: after about 20 failures in total lock the code until the sender resets it, and tell the sender. Consider an emailed one-time code as an option the sender can tick.

results.requirement: If the signer's email matches an existing account, the link still opens the document directly, and an account lockout never blocks signing.
results.evidence: find() in src/server/routes-sign.ts looks only at recipients and envelopes, never at accounts. Own check tests/out/audit-signer/api1.ts S1: created an account with the signer's address, drove its login into the 429 lock with 12 wrong passwords, then a cookie-less client opened the link (200), consented, completed (envelope completed) and downloaded the PDF (200).

results.requirement: The completion screen contains only a confirmation, a download button and a statement that a copy was emailed; no sign-up, trial or payment prompt appears anywhere in the signing flow.
results.evidence: The 'done' stage in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx shows the confirmation, 'A copy has been emailed to <address>', View and Download. A Playwright survey of every control on the consent, signing, sheet, adopt, review, done and reopened screens (phone1.mjs, two phone profiles) found no sign-up, login, trial, pricing or payment control. Screenshot tests/out/audit-signer/shots/p-13-done.png.
results.gap: The screen is not limited to those three things. It also shows the Impact card ('Everything paid to Sign&Grow goes to planting more. How we count'), and that link opens /impact in the same tab, a page with 'Start free', 'Sign in' and 'Start signing' buttons. So a signer who has just finished is one tap away from a sign-up call to action.
results.suggested_fix: src/components/sign/parts.tsx Impact(): on signing screens drop the sentence about payments and either remove the /impact link or point it at a methodology-only view without the public navigation, opened in a new tab.

results.requirement: Signing a document never adds the signer's address to a marketing list; signers receive transactional emails only.
results.evidence: There is no marketing list or newsletter mailer: the full table list (api1.ts S3) has none, and every sendMail call in src/server is tied to an envelope, an account or a support request. The signer's address is stored only on the recipients row and in the sender's own address book (contacts insert in sendEnvelope(), src/server/envelopes.ts). Own check S3: across send, reminder and completion the signer received exactly three emails (request, 'Reminder: …', 'Completed: …') and no user row was created for them.
results.gap: Note: each of those emails ends with the line 'Sent with Sign&Grow, where every dollar plants 10 mangrove trees with Treegens' (renderMail, src/server/mail.ts). Listed under overclaims against the 'no marketing' promise.
results.suggested_fix: Shorten the footer in emails to recipients to 'Sent with Sign&Grow' plus the help link.

results.requirement: A signing link stays valid until the document is completed, declined, voided or past the sender's deadline; there is no limit on the number of opens (test: a link opened 50 times still works).
results.evidence: Tokens have no expiry and no open counter (recipients.token; find() in src/server/routes-sign.ts). Repo test tests/trust.test.ts 'small things that stop people getting stuck' opens one link 50 times. Own checks: api1.ts S2, 600 opens in a row all 200; S5, a completed link still opened and downloaded after its dates were moved back to 2024; api3.ts P3, after expiry and reopening the same link worked with consent and typed values intact.
results.gap: Caveat, filed as a bug: all signing calls from one IP share a limit of 600 per 10 minutes. The 601st call returned 429, and so did a different signer with a different document on the same IP.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/routes-sign.ts find(): key the limit on token plus IP, or raise it well above what an office behind one address can produce.

results.requirement: If a link is invalid for any reason, the same page lets the signer verify with a one-time code to their email or phone and continue into the document in the same session, with no action by the sender.
results.evidence: src/components/sign/deadEnds.tsx: a replaced link (410) offers 'Email me the current link' (POST /public/links/resend), an unknown link (404) offers 'Email me my documents' (POST /public/links/find), both without the sender. Repo test 'lost and replaced links are recoverable without the sender'. Both screens seen in the browser (browser2.mjs D).
results.gap: There is no one-time code and no carrying on in the same session: the person has to go back to the inbox, and for a replaced link the new one goes to whoever holds the document now. For a recipient who was removed, or when the envelope is closed, the page still answers 'Sent.' although nothing is sent (api2.ts S9: 0 emails). A link whose envelope the sender deleted says 'It may have been cut short when it was copied', which is untrue. An expired document still needs the sender.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/routes-trust.ts: add a verify step that emails a 6-digit code to the recipient's address and, once typed on the same page, redirects to the current /sign/<token>. Let resendFromRetired() return why nothing was sent and have deadEnds.tsx say 'You were removed from this document' or 'This document was closed'. Keep a marker for deleted envelopes so the page can say the sender removed it.

results.requirement: Field values are saved as the signer enters them and restored when the signer returns after a timeout or on another device.
results.evidence: flush() in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx posts the values 1.5 s after each change, retries every 8 s on failure, and again when the tab is hidden or closed; POST /sign/:token/save in src/server/routes-sign.ts stores them. Repo test asserts 'saved values come back'. Browser check browser2.mjs A: typed text and consent were present on a second device with a fresh profile.
results.gap: The adopted signature does not travel. The autosave body holds only 'values' (captured in tests/out/audit-signer/browser2c.json), so on another device or in a new tab every signature and initials field comes back empty, and opening the second device also wipes the 'signed' mark on the server. The server already accepts signature_png on /save and tests/trust.test.ts line 419 asserts 'the chosen signature is kept for another device', but the page never sends it.
results.suggested_fix: page.tsx flush(): include signature_png and initials_png when they change (once, not on every keystroke). On a new device show the saved signature and ask for one confirming tap rather than emptying the fields.

results.requirement: The sender is notified automatically when a signer hits an expired or failed link.
results.evidence: noteDeadLink() in src/server/envelopes.ts emails the sender 'Could not open: …' when a signer opens an expired envelope (GET /sign/:token) and after three wrong access codes. Own check api2.ts S9: first open of an expired link sent 1 email. The repo tests only cover the access-code case.
results.gap: (a) It fires once per recipient for ever: after the sender reopened and the deadline passed again, the next open sent nothing, because dead_link_alerted_at is never cleared and is shared with the access-code alert. (b) Nothing is sent when the expired document has an access code not yet entered (the route returns before the notice). (c) Nothing for a replaced link (410) or an unknown link. (d) All of it is silent if the sender switched off 'When something needs you'.
results.suggested_fix: envelopes.ts: clear dead_link_alerted_at in extendEnvelope() and correctRecipient(). routes-sign.ts GET /sign/:token: call noteDeadLink before the `if (locked)` return. routes-trust.ts /public/links/resend: tell the sender when a retired link is used. Add tests for the expired case.

results.requirement: When a verification fails, the signer sees the specific reason (for example glare, blur, name mismatch, code expired) and how to fix it.
results.evidence: The only check is the sender's access code (POST /sign/:token/unlock in src/server/routes-sign.ts; locked screen in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx). Browser check browser2.mjs C: a wrong code shows 'That access code is not right. Check it and try again, or ask Demo Sender for the code.' with the sender's name and email on the same screen.
results.gap: After 8 tries in 15 minutes the message becomes 'Too many attempts. Please wait a bit and try again.' It does not say how long (15 minutes) or whom to ask, and the correct code is then refused with the same message, also from another device (api2.ts S10), because the limit is per document link, not per person trying.
results.suggested_fix: routes-sign.ts /unlock: count only failures, answer 429 with the minutes left and the sender's contact; page.tsx: show that text on the locked screen.

results.requirement: After two failed attempts the signer is offered an alternative method the sender pre-approved, and the sender is notified with the failure reason.
results.evidence: After the third wrong code the sender gets 'Could not open: …' naming the signer, the reason and the code (routes-sign.ts /unlock calling noteDeadLink). Repo test in tests/trust.test.ts; own check api2.ts S10 shows sender emails after tries 1, 2, 3 as 0, 0, 1.
results.gap: The sender hears after three failures, not two, and only once per recipient ever. The signer is offered no other method. The only way forward is to reach the sender through the mailto link; 'Ask the sender a question' is not available on the locked screen because /ask needs the code.
results.suggested_fix: Notify at the second failure. Let the sender tick a fallback per recipient (a one-time code emailed to that recipient) and offer it on the locked screen after two failures. Add an 'I do not have the code' button that emails the sender without needing the code.

results.requirement: The sender is charged only for successful verifications.
results.evidence: Nothing is charged per verification. Access codes are free, and a signature is only taken from the balance in completeRecipient() when the person actually signs (src/server/envelopes.ts, src/server/credits.ts, tests/billing.test.ts).

results.requirement: The signer can choose the one-time-code channel (SMS, voice call or email) with a visible resend timer; phone numbers are validated with country code when the sender enters them.
results.evidence: On purpose there is no one-time code, SMS or call, and no phone number is collected anywhere (no phone column in src/server/db.ts; src/app/security/page.tsx says 'we do not send codes by SMS or phone'), so undelivered codes and rejected numbers cannot happen.
results.gap: What remains is the cousin of this complaint: the access code only arrives if the sender passes it on. See the two requirements above.

results.requirement: Public-record quiz verification is not offered, and no biometric check is the only route.
results.evidence: A search of src for quiz, biometric, liveness, selfie or ID checks finds nothing. The only identity option in the schema (recipients.access_code), the API description and the editor is the access code. The certificate prints 'Identity check: Email link' or 'Email link and access code' (drawCertificate in src/server/pdf.ts), confirmed in a rendered certificate (tests/out/audit-signer/pdfshot.mjs).

results.requirement: The completion email attaches the signed PDF and audit certificate (or a non-expiring link when the file is too large to attach).
results.evidence: completeEnvelope() in src/server/envelopes.ts builds the PDF with its certificate and attaches it when under 8 MB. Own check api1.ts S15 with a stubbed mail transport: the signer's 'Completed:' email carried 'Attach me.pdf' (25,589 bytes, starts %PDF). A rendered signed file shows the certificate pages (pdfshot.mjs).
results.gap: Above 8 MB only the link is sent, and that link is not non-expiring: it returns 404 as soon as the sender deletes the envelope (api1.ts S4) or closes the account. With two signers on one address only one completion email goes out, carrying the first person's link. The over-8-MB path was not exercised.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/routes-envelopes.ts DELETE /envelopes/:id: for completed envelopes hide them from the sender instead of deleting the recipients and final PDF, so /sign/:token/download keeps working. In the completion email say plainly when the PDF was too large to attach.

results.requirement: A 'get my copy' page lets a signer enter the email they signed with, receive a one-time code and download the document with no account; it works for the full retention period, which is stated in the completion email.
results.evidence: /help#find-documents (FindDocuments in src/app/help/tools.tsx, POST /public/links/find, emailMyLinks() in src/server/envelopes.ts) needs no account. Repo test 'lost and replaced links are recoverable without the sender'. Own check api1.ts S5: works whatever the letter case, and a document completed 'in 2024' was found, opened and downloaded. The completion email states the rule: 'for as long as <sender> keeps their Sign&Grow account'.
results.gap: It emails links rather than giving a code and a download on the page. Left out of the list: documents the person has signed while others have not finished (S5: no email at all), anything past the 50 most recent, and anything the sender deleted (S4: nothing sent, yet the page says 'Check your inbox'). For two people on one address the entries are identical, with no names (api2.ts S6). The retention sentence is wrong when the sender deletes a single envelope.
results.suggested_fix: emailMyLinks(): also include envelopes still in progress where the recipient's own status is 'completed', add 'for <recipient name>' to each line, and page or raise the cap. Fix the deletion problem as above or change the email wording.

results.requirement: Download and print are available to the signer before, during and after signing, and no sender, branding or API setting can hide them.
results.evidence: Download and 'View or print' are on the consent screen, in the signing toolbar and menu, and on the done screen (src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx), served by GET /sign/:token/download. No account, brand or API setting touches them (PATCH /account takes only name, colour, logo and defaults). Own check api1.ts S13: 200 before consent, 200 inline, 200 after signing; the done-screen download returned application/pdf in the browser.
results.gap: For someone who has already signed, the copy disappears if the envelope later expires, is voided or is declined (403 'This envelope is closed', S13), or is deleted by the sender (404, S4). So a sender's action can still take the download away after signing, and the consent text 'You can download or print a copy at any time' is not always true.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/routes-sign.ts assertViewable(): let a recipient whose own status is 'completed' keep downloading what they signed, marked 'not completed' or 'voided', and keep it after the sender deletes the envelope.

results.requirement: Once an email address is verified, every document ever sent to or signed by that address is listed, regardless of when an account was created.
results.evidence: GET /inbox in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts lists by recipient address once the account's email is confirmed. Own check api1.ts S14: a document signed before the account existed appeared after confirming the address; unconfirmed accounts get nothing.
results.gap: Hard cap of 100 rows with no paging in the route or in src/app/app/inbox/page.tsx, so older documents cannot be reached. Envelopes the sender deleted vanish. Two people on one address see identical rows with no names.
results.suggested_fix: Add offset paging to /inbox and the page, and show the recipient name on each row.

results.requirement: Signing works in iOS Safari, Android Chrome and in-app mail browsers with no app install, and no sender or template setting can block phones.
results.evidence: No app, no device detection anywhere in src (no userAgent checks), and no sender or template setting about devices. bugs.title: Client IP is taken from a header the client controls (security)
bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/router.ts, handle(): ip = first entry of x-forwarded-for
bugs.detail: The left-most X-Forwarded-For value is trusted. Against the dev server, `curl -X POST -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 6.6.6.6, 7.7.7.7' …/api/sign/<token>/mute` wrote ip 6.6.6.6 into the audit trail. Two effects: a signer can put any address into the audit trail and certificate ('IP address' on the certificate), and every per-IP limit (signing calls, security-code checks, sign-up, support, find-my-documents per IP) can be sidestepped by changing the header (api1.ts S2: spoofed address got 200 while the real one was at 429). Behind a proxy that appends rather than overwrites, the first entry is still the client's.

bugs.title: Access codes: correct code locked out, any length accepted, guessable over days (security)
bugs.detail: The limit of 8 tries per 15 minutes is counted per recipient before the code is checked, so after 8 wrong tries by anyone holding the link the right code is refused too, from any device, with 'Too many attempts. Please wait a bit and try again.' (api2.ts S10; browser2.mjs C). There is no minimum length (a 1-character code was accepted) and no permanent lock, so a 4-digit code can be exhausted in under two weeks. The sender is emailed once, at the third failure, and never again. Each failure also adds a line to the audit trail.

An office or campus signing a bulk send together can reach this; the page then shows 'We could not open this just now' and autosave fails until the window passes.

results.requirement: The sender sees a per-recipient delivery status: sent, delivered, bounced (with the bounce reason), opened, or held.
results.evidence: Code: sendMail() in src/server/mail.ts records every email as queued/outbox/sent/failed with the mail server's error text; GET /envelopes/:id (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts) returns them as `deliveries`; EmailFact() and badge() in src/components/sender/Recipients.tsx show one line per recipient ('Handed to the mail server on…', 'Could not be sent: <error>', 'Opened on…'). results.gap: Only what happens at hand-over to the mail server is known. There is no 'delivered' and no real 'bounced': a bounce, quarantine or spam verdict that comes back later from the recipient's mail system is never received (no inbound webhook or bounce parsing anywhere in src/server). A failed send is not retried and the sender is not emailed about it; they only see it if they open the envelope. The audit trail and certificate still say 'Sent to recipient' when the email failed. 'Held' does not exist as a state.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/mail.ts: store the provider message id on `emails`; add a public, signed route (new file or routes-account.ts) that accepts the mail provider's delivery/bounce/complaint events and sets status delivered/bounced/complained with the reason. Show those in Recipients.tsx EmailFact, add them to WEBHOOK_EVENTS, call notifySender(e,'problems',…) on a bounce or failed send, and retry transient failures from cronTick(). In advance() write 'Email could not be sent' to the audit trail instead of 'Sent to recipient' when sendMail failed.
