results.evidence: Link half is there and works: POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts returns signUrl(r) and writes 'Signing link issued' to the audit trail; copy() and shareVia() in src/components/sender/Recipients.tsx give 'Copy link', 'Share on WhatsApp' and 'Share by text message' per recipient. Browser check (tests/out/audit-sender/ui2.mjs): clicking 'Copy link' put the same URL on the clipboard as the one in the signer's email.
results.gap: The service sends no SMS on any plan. 'Share by text message' only opens the sender's own phone messaging app (an sms: link). README 'What is not in it' and /security say SMS is not built. No automated test covers the recipient-view route.
results.suggested_fix: Decide whether SMS is in scope. If yes: add a phone column to recipients, an SMS provider call next to sendMail() in notifyRecipient() (src/server/envelopes.ts), and a delivery row per SMS. If no: keep the copy/share buttons and say on /help#not-received that text messages are sent from the sender's own phone. Either way add a test for POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view to tests/trust.test.ts.

results.requirement: If an outbound request is held for review, the sender is told immediately with the reason and expected time, nothing is sent to recipients until release, and the sender can cancel it.
results.evidence: There is no silent hold. sendEnvelope() in src/server/envelopes.ts either sends or refuses at once with the reason (403 unconfirmed email, 403 paused account, 429 daily limit, 422 looks like a scam). When an account is paused, reportAbuse() and POST /operator/accounts/:id (src/server/routes-trust.ts) email owners and admins. Check I ran (tests/out/audit-sender/a7-more.ts): after three reports the owner got 'Sending is paused on your Sign&Grow account' saying '3 different recipients reported…'. Test 'recipients can check that an email is genuine…' proves a paused account cannot send and can still export.
results.gap: No expected time is given anywhere (pause email, 403 message, help page). A pause does not stop everything: a paused account can still email new people by correcting an envelope that is out, and can still send reminders (probe a1-phishing.ts F: correction 200, new addresses mailed, reminders 2). A request refused as a scam has no release path: the message promises 'a person will clear it' but the operator queue has no such action. There is no per-request hold the sender could cancel.
results.suggested_fix: src/lib/policy.ts: add a review-time promise and quote it in the pause emails, the 403 text and /help#cannot-send. In correctEnvelope(), correctRecipient(), reassignRecipient() and remindEnvelope() refuse (or queue) any email to a new address while accounts.suspended_at is set. Turn the scam refusal into a real held state (envelopes.status='held', nothing sent, sender sees reason and a Cancel button) with a 'Release' action in src/app/app/operator/page.tsx.

results.requirement: The sender is alerted when a recipient has not opened the request within a configurable time (default 24 hours).
results.evidence: cronTick() in src/server/envelopes.ts emails the sender 'Not opened yet: …' once per recipient, with advice to copy the link or correct the address. Test 'small things that stop people getting stuck' proves it fires once. My probe a2-corrections.ts (c7): no alert at 25 h or 47 h, one alert at 49 h.
results.gap: The default is 48 hours, not 24. The time is one server-wide setting (UNOPENED_ALERT_HOURS); a sender cannot choose it (Settings has no such control, checked in the browser). The alert is skipped, and still marked as given, when the sender has 'When something needs you' emails off. Two bugs: after fixing an address with the quick 'Correct' dialog the alert fires within minutes because sent_at is not reset; after fixing an address in the editor it never fires for the new address because unopened_alerted_at is not reset.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts cronTick(): default 24 h and read a per-account value (new accounts.unopened_alert_hours, edited under Settings > Notifications in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx). In correctRecipient() set sent_at=now when the address changes; in correctEnvelope() and reassignRecipient() clear unopened_alerted_at. Do not set unopened_alerted_at when no email was actually sent to the sender.

results.requirement: Outbound mail passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC; the sender can edit the subject and message, and paid plans can send from their own verified domain.
results.evidence: Subject and message are editable per envelope (StepAdd in src/components/editor/StepAdd.tsx, stored by writeContent()) and appear in the email (notifyRecipient(); seen in the rendered email in ui2.mjs and in test 'recipients can check that an email is genuine…'). fromHeader() in src/server/mail.ts sends from the service's own MAIL_FROM address as '<name> via Sign&Grow' with Reply-To set to the sender, which is the shape that can pass DMARC.
results.gap: Nothing in the code or README checks, sets up or even mentions SPF, DKIM or DMARC; whether mail passes depends entirely on how MAIL_FROM's domain and the SMTP provider are configured, and nobody is warned if it does not. There is no sending from a customer's own verified domain on any plan (one global MAIL_FROM).
results.suggested_fix: Add a startup/operator check (shown on /app/operator) that looks up the SPF and DMARC TXT records and the DKIM selector for the MAIL_FROM domain and warns when they are missing; document the DNS records in README 'Configuration'. For own-domain sending: accounts.mail_domain plus a DNS verification step in routes-account.ts, and use it in fromHeader() for paid accounts.

results.requirement: Every signing email shows the verified sender name and organisation and a short code; a public page on our own domain accepts that code and confirms whether the request is genuine and who sent it.
results.evidence: notifyRecipient() in src/server/envelopes.ts passes the sender name, email and check_code to renderMail() (src/server/mail.ts), which prints 'Sent by <name> (<email>)', the account name and a 12-character code with 'type <host>/check yourself'. POST /public/check in src/server/routes-trust.ts and src/app/check/CheckForm.tsx answer genuine or not, with sender, account, recipient, subject and state. Test 'recipients can check that an email is genuine, stop reminders, and report a suspicious request' passes; I also looked at the rendered email (tests/out/audit-sender/email.png).
results.gap: Only the sender's email address is verified. The name and the organisation are whatever the sender typed: probe a1-phishing.ts B signed up as 'PayPal Billing', renamed the account 'PayPal' (PATCH /account, 200) and the email went out headed 'PayPal Billing sent you a document to sign' under a 'PayPal' brand line; /check would then show a green 'Genuine' with those names. A code that was replaced by a correction answers 'does not match any email we have sent… treat the email as fake' although the email was genuine (probe I). Without APP_URL the address printed for the check page follows a forged Host header.
results.suggested_fix: routes-account.ts PATCH /me and PATCH /account plus signup: refuse or flag names containing well-known brands for accounts without a verified domain; in renderMail() and CheckForm label the name as 'not verified by Sign&Grow' unless the sender's email domain is verified for that account. Keep retired codes (like retired_tokens) so POST /public/check can answer 'genuine, replaced by a newer email'. Refuse to start in production without APP_URL (src/server/util.ts baseUrl).

results.requirement: Every signing email has a 'Report this request' link that reaches a monitored abuse queue; a report can pause that sender's outbound mail pending review.
results.evidence: Reporting exists on the signing page: 'Report this request' in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx opens ReportDialog (src/components/sign/dialogs.tsx) which calls POST /sign/:token/report; reportAbuse() in src/server/envelopes.ts stores the report, emails ABUSE_EMAIL/SUPPORT_EMAIL when set, and pauses the account after reports from 3 different recipients (ABUSE_SUSPEND_AFTER). The queue is GET /operator/queue and src/app/app/operator/page.tsx, where an operator can also pause by hand. Test 'recipients can check that an email is genuine…' proves the pause, the queue and lifting it.
results.gap: The email itself has no report link (probe a1 J and browser check: the word 'report' does not occur in the email; the only link is 'Review and sign'). A wary recipient has to open the suspicious link, or find /help, to report. With neither ABUSE_EMAIL/SUPPORT_EMAIL nor OPERATOR_EMAILS set, a report is stored and nobody is told (probe K: 0 emails). The reporter gets no acknowledgement by email. A pause blocks new sends only: corrections to new addresses and reminders still go out (probe F). Reports an operator marks 'This was abuse' stop counting towards the automatic pause (a7-more.ts: two confirmed plus a third new report, not paused). Whether the queue is monitored is for the people running it.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/mail.ts renderMail(): add 'Report this request' pointing at a page on our own domain that takes the security code (for example /check?code=…&report=1) so nothing in the suspicious email has to be trusted. reportAbuse(): count upheld as well as open reports; email the reporter a receipt; log a loud warning at start-up when no abuse inbox and no operator is configured. Block correction and reminder emails while suspended_at is set.

results.requirement: New and free accounts are rate-limited on sends to external addresses until email plus payment identity or domain is verified, and the limits are published.
results.evidence: sendEnvelope() in src/server/envelopes.ts requires a confirmed email and, for unpaid accounts (free plan or free code) in their first 7 days, caps recipients at newAccountDailyRecipients() = 50 a day (src/lib/policy.ts). Test 'signup, session and CSRF protection' proves the email check; my probe a1-phishing.ts E got 200 for the first 50 and 429 for the 51st with a clear message.
results.gap: The cap is checked only when an envelope is first sent. Changing the addresses on an envelope that is out is not counted: probe E mailed 200 different addresses on day one from one new free account (three corrections of 50 addresses each, all 200 OK). After day 7 a free account has no limit at all, and viewers, approvers and copies cost no signatures, so probe G mailed 300 people in one go with billing on and nothing verified. The number is not on any public page: /help and /security say only 'a limited number of people a day'. Per-IP limits trust the first X-Forwarded-For value.
results.suggested_fix: Put one check in a helper used by sendEnvelope(), correctEnvelope(), correctRecipient() and reassignRecipient(): count distinct addresses emailed for the account in the last 24 h from the `emails` table. Keep a cap for every unpaid account until a payment or a verified domain exists, not just for 7 days. Print the numbers on src/app/help/page.tsx (#cannot-send) and src/app/security/page.tsx from src/lib/policy.ts.

results.requirement: Outbound requests are scanned for invoice and payment-lure patterns before delivery and held with notice to the sender if flagged.
results.evidence: looksLikeScam() in src/server/envelopes.ts flags a money word plus a phone number plus a brand name in the subject, message and document names; sendEnvelope() refuses with 422 and an explanation for unpaid accounts under 30 days old. Test 'new free accounts cannot send fake payment notices…' passes and my probe A reproduced the 422.
results.gap: The scan is easy to walk around (all in tests/out/audit-sender/a1-phishing.ts): B, put the brand in the sender name and account name instead of the subject (sent); C, put the whole lure in the per-recipient note, which is printed in the email (sent); D, send something clean, then correct the subject and message into 'PayPal invoice #4471… call +1 (888)…' and change the address: the victim received it, plus a reminder; H, any free account older than 30 days or any paid account on day one sends the documented scam unchecked. The words inside the PDF are never looked at although files.text holds them. A flagged request is refused, not held: there is nothing for a person to release, although the error, /help and /security say a person can clear it.
results.suggested_fix: Move the check into notifyRecipient() so every outgoing request, reminder and corrected request is scanned, over subject, message, recipient note, sender name, account name, document names and files.text. Apply it to every account without a verified payment or domain. On a hit set the envelope to a held state, tell the sender why, and add 'Release' and 'Reject' to the operator queue (routes-trust.ts, src/app/app/operator/page.tsx).

results.requirement: The published abuse address accepts mail and returns an acknowledgement (test: a message to it never bounces).
results.evidence: The published way to report is a form, not a mailbox: POST /public/support in src/server/routes-trust.ts (topic 'suspicious', linked from /help#unexpected and from /check) stores the message, shows a reference at once and emails the writer 'We got your message (REF)'. Test 'support is open to anyone, and an account can be closed for good' proves the storage, the reference and the acknowledgement email. SUPPORT_EMAIL is shown on /help when configured.
results.gap: No abuse address is published: ABUSE_EMAIL is only used as the destination for report notifications and never shown. Mail sent to SUPPORT_EMAIL is handled by whatever mailbox the operators set up; the software cannot acknowledge it or stop it bouncing. A report made from the signing page is acknowledged on screen only. Policy part: someone has to own a real abuse mailbox and read the queue; the README says so under 'Things to decide before launch'.
results.suggested_fix: Show ABUSE_EMAIL (falling back to SUPPORT_EMAIL) on src/app/help/page.tsx #unexpected and src/app/security/page.tsx #scams, or state plainly that the form is the abuse channel. Add an inbound-mail hook for that address that files the message into support_requests and sends the same acknowledgement. Operators: create the mailbox, set OPERATOR_EMAILS, and test it before launch.

results.requirement: Until the last signature, the sender can change a recipient's name, email, role or signing order without voiding and without losing signatures already collected.
results.evidence: correctEnvelope() and correctRecipient() in src/server/envelopes.ts (PUT /envelopes/:id and POST /envelopes/:id/correct) update recipients in place; writeContent() never touches finished people. Tests 'a sent envelope can be corrected without voiding it', 'lost and replaced links are recoverable without the sender' and 'small things that stop people getting stuck' pass. My probe a2-corrections.ts c1: after Ada signed, Ben's name, email, role (signer to approver) and order were all changed in one save: 200, envelope still 'sent', Ada still completed with her signature, chain intact, Ben re-invited at the new address.
results.gap: A changed signing order is saved but not enforced for someone who already has the document: probe c4 moved Ada behind Ben; both then had live links and Ada could still sign first (200). A person who has finished cannot have even a misspelled name fixed, and a request to do so answers 200 and silently does nothing (probe c1b). The audit entry for a correction made in the editor says only 'Now 3 recipients, 3 fields, 2 pages': the old and new address, role and order are not recorded.
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts correctEnvelope(): on an ordered envelope, when someone with status sent/viewed is no longer in the current turn after the change, set them back to pending and tell them it is not their turn yet. Return 409 (as the API description promises) when a finished person's details differ instead of ignoring them. Write one audit line per changed person, for example 'Ben Signer <ben@…> is now Benjamin Signer <benjamin@…>, approver, order 3'.

results.requirement: The sender can add or move fields or replace the document; only signers whose already-signed content changed are asked to sign again, and they are shown what changed.
results.evidence: Adding and moving fields for people who have not finished works at any time, and replacing the file works until the first person finishes: correctEnvelope() with lockedView()/askView() in src/server/envelopes.ts, 'Replace file' in src/components/editor/StepAdd.tsx. Probes: a3-fields-after-signature.ts (after Ada signed, a field added and one moved for Ben: 200, Ben got 'Updated:', Ada heard nothing); a2 c2 (document replaced before anyone signed: 200, same link, 'Updated:' email). Test 'a sent envelope can be corrected without voiding it' covers the lock.
results.gap: There is no sign-again flow. Once anyone has finished, replacing the document is refused (409, probe c2b) and the only way is to void and lose the signatures, which is the original complaint. Nobody is shown what changed: the notice is one fixed sentence ('changed this document after sending it. Please look at it again'). Worse, the lock has holes: the sender can still add their own words to pages already signed (bug 1 and 2), and a signer whose page is already open can finish on a swapped document without seeing it (bug 3).
results.suggested_fix: correctEnvelope(): allow a change to locked content by setting the affected finished signers back to 'sent' (keeping everyone else), with their earlier signature kept in the audit trail. Build a plain list of differences from lockedView()/askView() before and after (document replaced, pages, fields added, moved or removed) and put it in the 'Updated' email and in a banner on src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx. Send a version stamp with GET /sign/:token and require it on POST /sign/:token/complete.

results.requirement: Every correction emails the affected signers a 'this document was updated' notice, makes old links open the latest version, and is recorded in the audit trail.
results.evidence: correctEnvelope() sends notifyRecipient(…,'updated') to everyone who has the document and whose part changed, keeps their token, retires replaced tokens (retireToken(); the sign page offers the new link via resendFromRetired()), and writes 'Envelope corrected' to the hash-chained audit trail. Tests 'a sent envelope can be corrected without voiding it' and 'lost and replaced links are recoverable without the sender' pass. Probe a2 c5: the unchanged link showed the moved field at its new place.
results.gap: The audit entry is a count only ('Now 3 recipients, 6 fields, 2 pages'). It does not record a swapped address, a changed role, or that the document file was replaced (no old or new fingerprint). People who already signed are not told when something is added to the pages they signed (probe a4: Ada heard nothing until 'Completed'). A changed subject or message tells nobody. Nothing checks that a signer has seen the updated version before they finish (probe c3).
results.suggested_fix: src/server/envelopes.ts correctEnvelope(): write what changed into the audit detail (per person old to new, per document old SHA-256 to new, fields added/moved/removed per person). Notify finished signers when anything on a page they signed changes, or refuse it. Add the version check on /sign/:token/complete described above and clear viewed_at for people whose part changed so the certificate shows they opened the new version.

results.requirement: Corrections and resends never consume allowance or incur a charge.
results.evidence: Code: correctEnvelope() in src/server/envelopes.ts only asks for signatures when the correction adds signers (available() < 0); correctRecipient(), remindEnvelope(), resendFromRetired() and extendEnvelope() write nothing to the credits ledger; a signature is only deducted in completeRecipient(). Test: tests/billing.test.ts 'a new account has 3 signatures to try…' ('Fixing a name costs nothing', and a correction that adds a signer beyond the balance is refused and changes nothing). My check (tests/out/audit-sender/a2-corrections.ts c6, payments on): after a quick address fix, two reminders, an editor correction that changed an address and moved a field, and a deadline extension, the balance was 3 with 2 held before and after, and the ledger held only the welcome line.

results.requirement: Fields are bound to signer roles, so swapping the person in a role keeps every field's position, size and type.
results.evidence: Code: every field carries recipient_id (fields table in src/server/db.ts); writeContent() in src/server/envelopes.ts updates the recipient row in place; copyEnvelope() maps each template role to the new recipient and fills name and email by role name; patchRcp() in src/components/Editor.tsx changes the person without touching fields. Test: 'templates, bulk send and PowerForms' (a template role filled with different people sends and signs). My check (tests/out/audit-sender/a2-corrections.ts c8): a template with a signature, an optional checkbox, a date and a labelled dropdown with options was used twice with different people, and the person in one role was then swapped on the draft; type, page, x, y, width, height, label and options were identical every time.

results.requirement: 'Replace document, keep fields' is available, with fields anchored to nearby text so they follow the content when the file changes.
results.evidence: 'Replace file' exists per document in src/components/editor/StepAdd.tsx; replaceDoc() in src/components/Editor.tsx swaps the file and keeps every field (fields on a page that no longer exists move to the last page). Browser check (tests/out/audit-sender/ui1.mjs): 8 fields before, 8 after, toast 'File replaced. Your fields are where you left them. Check they still line up.'
results.gap: Fields are not anchored to anything. They keep their old page coordinates, so when the layout shifts they sit in the wrong place: in my run the replacement PDF had one paragraph added at the top and every field ended up off its blank (screenshot tests/out/audit-sender/ed-step2-after-replace.png). The sender has to drag each one again, which is the complaint. On a sent envelope the file can only be replaced until the first person finishes. No automated test covers replacing a file.
results.suggested_fix: src/components/Editor.tsx replaceDoc(): before swapping, read the text of the old and the new file with scanPdf() from src/lib/autoplace.ts, remember for each field the nearest label or line of text and its offset, find that text in the new file and move the field with it. List the fields that could not be matched so the sender checks only those. Add a unit test next to tests/autoplace.test.ts.

results.requirement: On upload the editor detects existing PDF form fields and signature, date and checkbox positions and proposes fields the sender can accept or adjust.
results.evidence: src/lib/autoplace.ts: findInWidgets() turns PDF form fields (text, checkbox, radio, dropdown, signature) into fields; findInText() finds labels with a blank ('Signature: ____', 'Date: ____', name, title, company, email, initials) and {{tags}}. findForMe() in src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx adds them in one undoable step and never stacks on an existing field. Tests 1 to 9 in tests/autoplace.test.ts pass, including a real PDF read with pdf.js. Browser check (ui1.mjs): 'Found 6 places. Added 4 fields for Ada Sponsor. Undo takes them away again. 2 already had a field.'
results.gap: It does not run on upload: the sender has to go to step 2 and press 'Find fields for me'. Checkboxes are only found when they are real PDF form fields or {{checkbox}} tags; boxes drawn in the text ('[ ] I agree', '☐ Yes ☐ No', '( ) Monthly') are not detected (tests/out/audit-sender/a7-more.ts). Scanned documents give nothing, which the editor does say.
results.suggested_fix: src/components/Editor.tsx addFiles(): after an upload finishes, run scanPdf()+findFields() and show 'We found N places for fields. Add them?' on step 1 or on entering step 2. src/lib/autoplace.ts findInText(): recognise ☐, □, [ ], ( ) and small empty squares in front of text as checkbox or radio positions, with tests.

results.requirement: Dragging a field always moves it; copying is a separate action; undo and redo work; templates autosave with version history; any sent or draft document can be duplicated.
results.evidence: drag() in src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx only copies when Alt is held; dup(), Ctrl/Cmd+D and 'Copy to every page' are separate actions; useHistory() in src/components/editor/history.ts gives undo and redo; the autosave effect and save() in src/components/Editor.tsx run for drafts and templates; copyEnvelope() and POST /envelopes/:id/clone duplicate anything. Browser checks (ui1.mjs, ui3.mjs): one drag moved the field and the count stayed 7; 15 quick drags, still 7; undo moved it back and redo restored it; Alt+drag made 8; a template name typed in the editor was on the server 3 seconds later with 'All changes saved'. Probe a2 c8c: clone worked from draft, sent, completed, voided, declined and expired, with all fields and no signer-entered values.
results.gap: There is no version history for templates (or anything else): no table, no screen, no way back. A save replaces the whole template, and nothing detects a stale save: in tests/out/audit-sender/a6-misc.ts one team member saved 6 fields, a colleague's older editor then saved, got 200, and 5 fields were gone for good. Undo covers fields only; removing a recipient deletes their fields and cannot be undone (there is a confirmation first).
results.suggested_fix: src/server/db.ts: add envelope_versions (envelope_id, saved_at, saved_by, snapshot JSON); saveDraft() writes a snapshot when a template changes (at most one per editing session or per few minutes) and src/app/app/templates/page.tsx offers 'Earlier versions' with restore. PUT /envelopes/:id: accept the updated_at the editor loaded and answer 409 when the draft has changed since, so one editor cannot silently overwrite another.

results.requirement: A pixel-accurate 'preview as signer' is available before sending, and the date format is selectable per field.
results.evidence: Date format: five formats can be chosen per envelope or template (DATE_FORMATS in src/lib/dates.ts, the select in src/components/editor/StepAdd.tsx, envelopes.date_format, used by fieldDisplayValue() in src/server/pdf.ts and by the signing page). Test 'public forms do not multiply envelopes, and dates follow the chosen format' passes. So the date is not tied to the account's region.
results.gap: There is no preview as signer at all: the review step (src/components/editor/StepReview.tsx) lists people and field counts and has only 'Back' and 'Send' (browser check ui1.mjs, screenshot ed-step3.png). The only preview is 'Preview PDF' on the envelope page, which shows the flat PDF without the fields a signer would fill. The date format is per envelope, not per field: the fields table has no format column and the field settings panel has no such control.
results.suggested_fix: Add an authenticated GET /envelopes/:id/preview?recipient_id= that returns the same shape as GET /sign/:token for a draft, and a 'Preview as <name>' button in StepReview that renders the real signing components from src/components/sign read-only. Add fields.date_format (null means the envelope's format), a select in the field settings of StepFields.tsx for date fields, and pass it to fieldDisplayValue().

bugs.title: A signer does not see sender-written text assigned to another signer, but it is printed on the PDF they both signed
bugs.where: src/server/routes-sign.ts GET /sign/:token (`others` only shows a field once its owner has finished); src/server/pdf.ts drawField()
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a8-hidden-text.ts. Send to Ada and Ben at once. Give Ben a read-only text field with the value 'Ada also owes a fee of 5000 dollars'. Ada's signing data (fields and others) does not contain the sentence; she signs; Ben signs; the completed PDF contains the sentence. A read-only prefilled field is the sender's wording, like a note, and must be shown to everyone before they sign.

bugs.title: After someone has signed, the sender can still add words to the pages they signed
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts lockedView() and writeContent(); src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx (only notes are blocked)
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a4-text-after-signature.ts. Ada signs. The sender corrects the envelope and adds a read-only text field for Ben, 'The price is changed to 1 dollar', just above Ada's signature: PUT /envelopes/:id answers 200. Ada is told nothing until 'Completed'. Ben signs and the final PDF carries the sentence with both signatures. The audit trail says only 'Envelope corrected: Now 3 recipients, 6 fields, 2 pages'. Notes are refused with 409 in the same situation, so this is the same thing under another field type. Reachable from the editor too (Text field, Prefilled value, Read only).

bugs.title: A signer can finish on a document that was swapped while their page was open
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts completeRecipient() and correctEnvelope(); src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx complete()
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a2-corrections.ts c3. The signer opens the link and consents (their browser shows version one). The sender replaces the PDF with a different contract and moves the signature field (PUT 200). The signer presses Finish with the page they already had: 200, envelope completed, signature applied to the new document. The server keeps no record of which version a signer saw and /complete carries none. The sender can even time this, because the envelope page shows 'Opened' and how many fields are filled in.

bugs.title: The fake-payment-notice filter is bypassed three simple ways
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts looksLikeScam(), called only from sendEnvelope()
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a1-phishing.ts. B: sign up as 'PayPal Billing', rename the account 'PayPal', subject 'Invoice #4471', message with the amount and a phone number: sent, headed 'PayPal Billing sent you a document to sign' under a 'PayPal' brand line. C: put the lure in the recipient note, which the email prints as 'Note for you: …': sent. D: send a clean envelope, then PUT a correction with subject 'PayPal invoice #4471', the phone message and a new address: the victim gets it, and a reminder with the same subject. Also (H) the filter never runs for free accounts older than 30 days or for any paid account.

bugs.title: The new-account daily limit does not count corrections, and free accounts have no limit after a week
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts sendEnvelope() (limit), correctEnvelope() and correctRecipient() (no limit)
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a1-phishing.ts E and G. A brand-new free account sends one envelope to 50 viewers (allowed), is refused a 51st recipient (429), then changes all 50 addresses on the envelope that is out three times: each save is 200 and 200 different addresses were mailed on day one. With payments on, a free account 8 days old sent 6 envelopes to 50 viewers each (300 people) using 0 signatures, because viewers, approvers and copies are free and nothing else limits them.

bugs.title: A paused account can still email new people
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts correctEnvelope(), correctRecipient(), remindEnvelope() (none checks accounts.suspended_at)
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a1-phishing.ts F. With suspended_at set, a new send is refused (403) but: PUT correction that changes an address and adds a recipient is 200 and both new addresses are mailed; POST /envelopes/:id/correct to a third address is 200 and mailed; POST /remind sends reminders. A sender paused for phishing keeps a working channel through any envelope that was already out.

bugs.title: Without APP_URL, a forged Host header rewrites the links in outgoing emails (password reset takeover)
bugs.detail: Reproduce on a server started without APP_URL: curl -X POST /api/auth/forgot -H 'X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example' -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' with a victim's address. The reset email I captured linked to https://evil.example/reset?token=…. The base address is a process-wide value taken from the latest request, so signing links, 'type <host>/check' in signing emails and emails sent by the timer can all be pointed at another site. README says to set APP_URL in production, but nothing enforces it.

bugs.title: Quick 'Correct' lets other people sign without signatures on the balance, then free self-signing is blocked
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts correctRecipient() (no balance check), sendEnvelope() (`need > before` with a negative balance)
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a6-misc.ts P3 (payments on). Send an envelope to your own address (free), then POST /envelopes/:id/correct to change the address to a client; the client signs and a signature is deducted. Four clients signed on a balance of 3, leaving -1. Sending many self-addressed envelopes first and correcting them afterwards scales this without limit. Once the balance is negative, even a self-signed envelope is refused with 'This needs 0 signatures and you have 0 left', which contradicts 'Signing your own documents stays free'.

bugs.title: A stale save silently wipes a colleague's work on a shared template
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a6-misc.ts P11. Ann and Bob both open the same template. Ann adds 5 fields and saves (6 fields). Bob's editor, loaded earlier, saves a renamed subject: 200, and the template is back to 1 field. No warning, no version to restore. The same happens with two tabs.

bugs.title: /check tells the holder of a genuine email to treat it as fake after the sender corrects an address or role
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a1-phishing.ts I. The code in the first email is genuine before the correction and 'genuine: false' after it. The page then says 'Code … does not match any email we have sent' and 'treat the email as fake', with a small note about corrections underneath. Old codes are not kept, so a real email cannot be told apart from a forged one.

bugs.title: Reports an operator confirms as abuse stop counting towards the automatic pause
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts reportAbuse() counts only status='open'; POST /operator/reports/:id in src/server/routes-trust.ts
bugs.detail: Reproduce: tests/out/audit-sender/a7-more.ts. Two recipients report a sender; the operator clicks 'This was abuse' on both; a third recipient reports: the account is not paused, because only open reports are counted. Confirming abuse makes the automatic pause less likely unless the operator also presses 'Pause this sender'.

bugs.title: The audit trail does not say what a correction changed
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts correctEnvelope() audit(…'Envelope corrected', 'Now N recipients, M fields, P pages')
bugs.detail: Seen in a2-corrections.ts c1 and a3: swapping a signer's address, changing a role, replacing the PDF or adding fields all leave the same kind of line with counts only. The old address and the old document fingerprint are not recorded anywhere, so the certificate cannot show who was removed or that the file was replaced. The quick 'Correct' route does log old and new values.

bugs.title: 'Not opened yet' alert fires at the wrong time after an address is corrected
bugs.where: src/server/envelopes.ts correctRecipient() (sent_at kept), correctEnvelope() and reassignRecipient() (unopened_alerted_at kept), cronTick()
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a2-corrections.ts c7. Quick-correct an address on a request that is more than 48 hours old: the sender is told '… has not opened your document' at the next timer run, minutes after the new email went out. Correct the address in the editor instead: the sender is never alerted about the new address. Also (a6 P8) a sender who is a signer on their own envelope gets the alert about themselves.

bugs.title: Changing the signing order leaves the earlier signer active
bugs.detail: Reproduce: a2-corrections.ts c4. Ordered envelope, Ada has it. Move Ada to second and Ben to first: 200; Ben is invited, Ada keeps status 'sent' and can still complete first. The new order is not enforced for the person who already had the document.

bugs.title: API answers 200 while ignoring or dropping parts of the request
bugs.detail: a2-corrections.ts c1b: a correction that changes a finished signer's email returns 200 and silently changes nothing (the API description says 409). a6-misc.ts P13: creating an envelope with three fields, one with a mistyped recipient id and one with an unknown type, returns 200 with one field kept and no warning.

bugs.title: Failed emails are not retried and the record still says 'Sent to recipient'
bugs.detail: tests/out/audit-sender/a5-delivery.ts: with the mail server refusing connections the send answers 200, the recipient is 'sent', the audit trail (and so the certificate) says 'Sent to recipient', nothing tries again and the sender gets no email about it. A row left 'queued' after a crash is shown as 'Waiting to go out' although nothing will send it.

bugs.title: Per-address rate limits trust the first X-Forwarded-For value
bugs.where: src/server/router.ts handle() (`ip`), used by rateLimit() callers such as signup, /public/check, /public/support
bugs.detail: The client address is the first value of X-Forwarded-For. Unless the proxy in front overwrites that header, a caller picks their own 'address' per request and the limits on sign-ups (10 an hour), security-code checks and public forms do not bind. My probes got past the sign-up limit simply by changing that header between accounts.

overclaims.where: README.md ('new free accounts … cannot send fake payment notices'); src/app/security/page.tsx ('Fake payment notices are stopped')
overclaims.claim: A new free account cannot send something that reads like a payment notice from a well-known brand with a phone number to call.
overclaims.reality: It can, three ways shown in tests/out/audit-sender/a1-phishing.ts: brand in the sender and account name, lure in the recipient note, or correct a clean envelope into the lure after sending. Only the exact pattern in the subject, message or file name at first send is caught.

overclaims.where: src/server/envelopes.ts sendEnvelope() error text; src/app/help/page.tsx #cannot-send ('write to us and a person will clear it'); src/app/security/page.tsx ('A person can clear a genuine one')
overclaims.claim: If a flagged payment notice is genuine, a person will clear it.
overclaims.reality: The operator queue (src/server/routes-trust.ts, src/app/app/operator/page.tsx) can close help requests, mark reports and pause or unpause accounts. Nothing lets anyone clear or release a flagged envelope; the sender stays blocked until the account is 30 days old or paid.

overclaims.where: src/app/security/page.tsx #scams ('These checks run on every send', 'New free accounts have a daily limit')
overclaims.claim: The anti-scam checks run on every send, and a new free account can only send to a limited number of people a day.
overclaims.reality: The checks run only when an envelope is first sent. Corrections and reminders are not checked: one new free account mailed 200 different people on day one by changing addresses on an envelope that was out.

overclaims.where: src/app/security/page.tsx ('new sends from it stop until a person has reviewed it'); pause email in src/server/envelopes.ts reportAbuse(); src/app/app/operator/page.tsx ('Pausing only stops new sends')
overclaims.claim: When an account is paused, sending from it stops until a person has reviewed it.
overclaims.reality: A paused account can still email people it has never contacted, by changing or adding recipients on any envelope that is already out, and can still send reminders (a1-phishing.ts F).

overclaims.where: src/app/help/page.tsx #fix-after-sending; src/app/developers/page.tsx #correct; src/server/openapi.ts PUT /envelopes/{id}; envelope page ('what they signed is locked')
overclaims.claim: Once someone has finished, the documents and what that person signed are locked.
overclaims.reality: The sender can still put new wording on those pages as a read-only text field for a remaining signer; it is printed on the completed PDF and the person who already signed is not told (a4-text-after-signature.ts).

overclaims.where: src/app/developers/page.tsx ('A call that touches one of them returns 409 and changes nothing'); src/server/openapi.ts PUT /envelopes/{id}
overclaims.claim: A correction that touches a finished person's name, email, role or order returns 409.
overclaims.reality: Changing a finished signer's name or email returns 200 and is silently ignored (a2-corrections.ts c1b). Only moved fields, notes and documents give 409.

overclaims.where: src/app/check/CheckForm.tsx ('This email is real … Sent by <name>, <account>', badge 'Genuine'); src/server/mail.ts ('We will tell you who sent it')
overclaims.claim: The check page tells you who sent the email.
overclaims.reality: It repeats the name and organisation the sender typed. Only the email address was confirmed. An account named 'PayPal' with a user named 'PayPal Billing' gets the same green 'Genuine' result.

overclaims.where: src/app/check/CheckForm.tsx ('Code … does not match any email we have sent')
overclaims.claim: An unrecognised code means we never sent that email.
overclaims.reality: A code from a real email stops matching as soon as the sender corrects that recipient's address or role or the signer hands the document on, because old codes are overwritten (a1-phishing.ts I).

overclaims.where: src/app/security/page.tsx #proof ('Every step is recorded … corrections'); certificate audit trail (src/server/pdf.ts)
overclaims.claim: Corrections are written to the audit trail.
overclaims.reality: Only the fact and three counts are written ('Now 3 recipients, 6 fields, 2 pages'). Which address was replaced, that the document file was swapped, or what text was added is not recorded.

overclaims.where: Audit trail and certificate of completion: 'Sent to recipient' (src/server/envelopes.ts advance())
overclaims.claim: The request was sent to the recipient at that time.
overclaims.reality: The line is written before and regardless of the email result. With the mail server refusing, or with no mail server configured, the record still says 'Sent to recipient' (a5-delivery.ts).

overclaims.where: src/app/help/page.tsx #unexpected and src/app/check/CheckForm.tsx ('Every report goes to a person'); src/components/sign/dialogs.tsx ('A person reads every report')
overclaims.claim: Every report reaches a person.
overclaims.reality: A report is stored. It is emailed to someone only if ABUSE_EMAIL or SUPPORT_EMAIL is set, and visible in the queue only to addresses in OPERATOR_EMAILS (default nobody). With none set, nothing is sent and nobody can see it (a1-phishing.ts K), and the server gives no warning about that at start-up.

overclaims.where: src/server/envelopes.ts outOfSignatures() ('Signing your own documents stays free')
overclaims.claim: Signing your own documents is always free.
overclaims.reality: With a negative balance (reachable through the quick-correct gap) a self-signed envelope is refused with 'This needs 0 signatures and you have 0 left' (a6-misc.ts P3).
